$comment: Policy for scripts/gate_microservice_events.py.
knownUnhandled is a RATCHET, not an allowlist. A service is only ever REMOVED
from it. A new service missing the required events fails the gate immediately,
so the debt below can shrink but never grow. The gate also fails if a listed
service starts handling its events and is not removed here in the same PR —
without that, the list rots into a permanent exemption nobody revisits.
The seven entries below were measured on 2026-09-14, when the gate was written:
12 structurally-real microservices, of which 5 consumed identity lifecycle
events and 7 did not. Run `python3 scripts/gate_microservice_events.py --report`
before trusting that count — it drifts as services are fixed.
RESOLVED, config-service (2026-10-04). It subscribes to
identity.org.deleted and identity.user.deleted and cascades both
(services/config-service/src/events/): a deleted org or user no longer
strands config_values overrides, and a hard-deleted user's id is redacted
from config_history under right-to-erasure (migration 005). The CREATED
pair is declared not-applicable rather than stubbed: config_values is a
SPARSE override store, so a brand-new org or user needs no rows at all --
resolution walks platform -> portal -> org -> user and inherits
(src/resolver/resolve.ts). An empty created-handler would clear the ratchet
while seeding nothing, which is precisely the 'looks handled and seeds
nothing' failure the gate rejects one branch down. The owner decision
(2026-10-04) was to carve the per-topic notApplicable exemption below
rather than leave a correct service on the debt ratchet forever.
notApplicable is per-topic, reason-mandatory (>= 40 chars), may never cover
all four events for one service, and is mutually exclusive with
knownUnhandled and exempt -- enforced by gate_microservice_events.py. It is
a signed, greppable statement a reviewer can disagree with, not the silence
a knownUnhandled entry carries.
Still on the ratchet, and why: email/sms/payment hold NO per-entity rows
yet (provider proxies) and handle nothing today -- they are candidates for
the same notApplicable treatment, but only once each actually handles the
DELETED pair (no sparse store is exempt from delete: a row it can write, it
can strand). devportal-service (core_tables) and notification-service
(per-user preferences) are REAL seed debt, not not-applicable. selection-
list-service is org-scoped + lazily populated and handles the deleted pair
already; it is a notApplicable candidate on the created pair in a later PR.
Run `python3 scripts/gate_microservice_events.py --report` before trusting
any of this -- it drifts as services are fixed.

config-service.identity.org.created: config_values is a sparse override store; a new org needs zero rows -- resolution inherits platform->portal->org->user (src/resolver/resolve.ts). An empty seed handler would be the vacuous-pass the gate rejects.
config-service.identity.user.created: config_values is a sparse override store; a new user needs zero rows -- unset keys resolve to the inherited scope (src/resolver/resolve.ts). An empty seed handler would be the vacuous-pass the gate rejects.

exempt.name: core
exempt.reason: Shared library, not a deployable service — it has no Dockerfile, so discovery already rejects it. Listed explicitly so a future Dockerfile does not silently enrol it without a decision.
